records.source: לַכֹּ֖ל זְמָ֑ן וְעֵ֥ת לְכָל־חֵ֖פֶץ תַּ֥חַת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ס
records.gloss: For everything [there is] an appointed time, and a time for every matter under the heavens.
pieces: There is a set time for everything, \q a time for every matter under the heavens:

L.1: For everything [there is] an appointed time, \q and a time for every matter under the heavens:

R.1: Everything has its own time. \q There is a time for every activity in this world:

decisions.choice: verses 1-8: a poem of times
decisions.reason: After the heading line, fourteen pairs of opposites follow, from birth and death (verse 2) to war and peace (verse 8). Each pair is set in a balanced line, and the poem is set in lines; the rest of the chapter is reflective prose.

decisions.choice: appointed time: a fixed or set time
decisions.reason: The word (zeman) is a later Hebrew word for a set time or date (Nehemiah 2:6; Esther 9:27).

decisions.choice: time: the right moment or occasion for something
decisions.reason: The word ('et) is a time that fits what happens in it. It is said twenty-eight times in verses 2-8. Verse 11 says that God has made everything fitting in its time; verse 14 that what God does lasts. People live within times they do not set.

decisions.choice: matter: an activity or affair
decisions.reason: The word (chefets) first means delight or desire; in this book it means any matter or business people take up (3:17; 5:7; 8:6).

decisions.choice: in this world
decisions.reason: Readable's wording for "under the heavens" and "under the sun" (see 1:3, 1:13).

decisions.choice: a colon at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The list of times that follows hangs on this line, so each level closes it with a colon and sets the pairs of verses 2-8 as one list.

records.heading: A time for everything

records.source: עֵ֥ת לָלֶ֖דֶת וְעֵ֣ת לָמ֑וּת עֵ֣ת לָטַ֔עַת וְעֵ֖ת לַעֲק֥וֹר נָטֽוּעַ׃
records.gloss: A time to bear and a time to die; a time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted.
pieces: a time to give birth, a time to die, \q a time to plant, a time to root up what was planted,

L.2: a time for giving birth and a time for dying, \q a time for planting and a time for uprooting what is planted;

R.2: a time for birth and a time for death, \q a time for planting and a time for pulling up plants,

decisions.choice: to give birth: the start of a life
decisions.reason: The verb (yalad) is active, "to bear a child". Set beside "to die", it stands for the start of life as death stands for its end; many render it "to be born".

decisions.choice: birth and death first: the two times no one chooses
decisions.reason: The list opens with the beginning and end of life, which no person sets for themselves, and the second pair takes the same shape in the life of plants.

decisions.choice: a time for giving birth and a time for dying
alternatives: a time to give birth and a time to die
decisions.reason: Through verses 2-7 Literal renders each Hebrew "to" with a verb (le- with the infinitive) as "for ...ing", which shows the form and keeps the Hebrew "and" between the two halves of each pair.

decisions.choice: a time to give birth, a time to die
alternatives: a time to give birth and a time to die
decisions.reason: Through verses 2-8 Balanced sets the two halves of each pair side by side without "and", as English lists often do; the Hebrew joins them with "and", which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: a time for birth and a time for death
alternatives: a time to bear and a time to die
decisions.reason: Readable uses nouns for the first pair, which reads simply; it says the same (m1).

records.source: עֵ֤ת לַהֲרוֹג֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִרְפּ֔וֹא עֵ֥ת לִפְר֖וֹץ וְעֵ֥ת לִבְנֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: A time to kill and a time to heal; a time to break down and a time to build.
pieces: a time to kill, a time to heal, \q a time to pull down, a time to build up,

L.3: a time for killing and a time for healing, \q a time for tearing down and a time for building;

R.3: a time for killing and a time for making well, \q a time for knocking down and a time for building up,

decisions.choice: break down: break through or pull down a wall
decisions.reason: The verb (parats) is used of breaking through or tearing down walls (Isaiah 5:5; Nehemiah 4:1). Building is its opposite (Jeremiah 1:10 uses like pairs).

decisions.choice: kill: put to death, in war or by sentence
decisions.reason: The verb (harag) is a general word for killing. The poem names it as one of the times of human life, without saying when it is right.

records.source: עֵ֤ת לִבְכּוֹת֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂח֔וֹק עֵ֥ת סְפ֖וֹד וְעֵ֥ת רְקֽוֹד׃
records.gloss: A time to weep and a time to laugh; a time of mourning and a time of dancing.
pieces: a time to cry, a time to laugh, \q a time to lament, a time to dance,

L.4: a time for weeping and a time for laughing, \q a time for wailing and a time for dancing;

R.4: a time for crying and a time for laughing, \q a time for grieving and a time for dancing,

decisions.choice: wail: mourn aloud for the dead
decisions.reason: The verb (safad) is the loud lament for the dead, often with beating the breast (Genesis 23:2; Zechariah 12:10).

decisions.choice: dance: skip or leap for joy
decisions.reason: The verb (raqad) is to skip or leap (Psalm 114:4; 1 Chronicles 15:29). Mourning and dancing are the funeral and the wedding feast.

records.source: עֵ֚ת לְהַשְׁלִ֣יךְ אֲבָנִ֔ים וְעֵ֖ת כְּנ֣וֹס אֲבָנִ֑ים עֵ֣ת לַחֲב֔וֹק וְעֵ֖ת לִרְחֹ֥ק מֵחַבֵּֽק׃
records.gloss: A time to throw stones and a time to gather stones; a time to embrace and a time to be far from embracing.
pieces: a time to scatter stones, a time to gather stones, \q a time to embrace, a time to hold back from embracing,

L.5: a time for throwing away stones and a time for gathering stones, \q a time for embracing and a time for keeping far from embracing;

R.5: a time for throwing stones away and a time for gathering them, \q a time for hugging and a time for not hugging,

decisions.choice: throwing away and gathering stones: the meaning is uncertain
alternatives: clearing a field of stones, and gathering stones to build
spoiling an enemy's field with stones (2 Kings 3:19, 25)
a picture of sexual relations, matching the next line
decisions.reason: The pair is not explained. Farmers cleared stones from fields (Isaiah 5:2) and gathered stones to build walls and houses; an army could ruin a field by throwing stones on it (2 Kings 3:19, 25). Some early Jewish interpreters read it as a picture of a husband and wife coming together or keeping apart, which would match the embracing of the next line. The text does not say which is meant.

decisions.choice: embrace: hold someone in the arms
decisions.reason: The verb (chavaq) is used of a loving embrace (Song 2:6) and of greeting (Genesis 29:13). The second half is literally "a time to be far from embracing".

decisions.choice: hugging ... not hugging
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words.

records.source: עֵ֤ת לְבַקֵּשׁ֙ וְעֵ֣ת לְאַבֵּ֔ד עֵ֥ת לִשְׁמ֖וֹר וְעֵ֥ת לְהַשְׁלִֽיךְ׃
records.gloss: A time to seek and a time to lose; a time to keep and a time to throw away.
pieces: a time to search, a time to give up as lost, \q a time to keep, a time to throw away,

L.6: a time for seeking and a time for losing, \q a time for keeping and a time for throwing away;

R.6: a time for looking for things and a time for giving them up as lost, \q a time for keeping and a time for throwing away,

decisions.choice: lose: give up as lost
decisions.reason: The verb ('abad) in this form can mean to destroy, but beside "seek" it means to give something up for lost, to stop looking for it.

records.source: עֵ֤ת לִקְר֨וֹעַ֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִתְפּ֔וֹר עֵ֥ת לַחֲשׁ֖וֹת וְעֵ֥ת לְדַבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: A time to tear and a time to sew; a time to be silent and a time to speak.
pieces: a time to tear, a time to stitch together, \q a time to stay silent, a time to speak,

L.7: a time for tearing and a time for sewing, \q a time for keeping silent and a time for speaking;

R.7: a time for tearing cloth and a time for sewing it, \q a time for keeping quiet and a time for speaking,

decisions.choice: tear and sew: perhaps the tearing of clothes in grief
decisions.reason: People tore their clothes as a sign of grief or shock (Genesis 37:34; 2 Samuel 1:11), and in time the garment was sewn again. The pair may also mean any tearing and mending.

decisions.choice: silent and speak: as in Proverbs
decisions.reason: Silence fits grief (Job 2:13) and is often wise (Proverbs 17:28); there is also a word in its time (Proverbs 15:23).

records.source: עֵ֤ת לֶֽאֱהֹב֙ וְעֵ֣ת לִשְׂנֹ֔א עֵ֥ת מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְעֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם׃ס
records.gloss: A time to love and a time to hate; a time of war and a time of peace.
pieces: a time to love, a time to hate, \q a time for war, a time for peace.

L.8: a time for loving and a time for hating, \q a time of war and a time of peace.

R.8: a time for loving and a time for hating, \q a time for war and a time for peace.

decisions.choice: war and peace: the list ends with two nouns
decisions.reason: The first thirteen pairs use verbs; the last uses two nouns, "war" and "peace", which close the poem and sum up the life of nations. Love and hate, war and peace, are set in reverse order, so that the poem ends on peace.

records.source: מַה־יִּתְרוֹן֙ הָֽעוֹשֶׂ֔ה בַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר ה֥וּא עָמֵֽל׃
records.gloss: What [is] the advantage of the one working in that which he [is] toiling?
pieces: What do workers gain from all their hard work?

L.9: What gain [has] the worker from that at which {{gender:they toil|he toils}}?

R.9: So what good does all their hard work do for the people who work?

decisions.choice: what gain: the question of 1:3 again
decisions.reason: After the poem of times, Qoheleth asks his opening question again (1:3). If every time is set, what does human toil add?

decisions.choice: gain: what is left over (see 1:3)
decisions.reason: The word (yitron) is the book's word for lasting gain.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: gain ... hard work (B); what good ... hard work (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for yitron and 'amal (see 1:3).

records.heading: The task God has given

records.source: רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־הָֽעִנְיָ֗ן אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֧ן אֱלֹהִ֛ים לִבְנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם לַעֲנ֥וֹת בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: I have seen the business which God has given to the sons of humankind to be busy with it.
pieces: I have seen the task God has given human beings to keep them busy.

L.10: I have seen the task that God has given to the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}} to be occupied with.

R.10: I have seen the work God has given people to keep them busy.

decisions.choice: the task God has given: as in 1:13
decisions.reason: The words repeat 1:13, without the word "evil". Here the task is set within the times God has made (verses 1-8, 11).

decisions.choice: {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}
decisions.reason: The phrase means human beings, men and women; the gender setting gives the inclusive form by default (see 1:13).

records.source: אֶת־הַכֹּ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה יָפֶ֣ה בְעִתּ֑וֹ גַּ֤ם אֶת־הָעֹלָם֙ נָתַ֣ן בְּלִבָּ֔ם מִבְּלִ֞י אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹא־יִמְצָ֣א הָאָדָ֗ם אֶת־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֛ה אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים מֵרֹ֥אשׁ וְעַד־סֽוֹף׃
records.gloss: The all he has made beautiful in its time; also eternity he has put in their heart, without that not will find the man the work which God has done from beginning and to end.
pieces: God has made everything fitting in its own time. He has also put a sense of eternity in their hearts, but people still cannot discover the work God has done from start to finish.

L.11: Everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made beautiful in its time; also {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has put eternity in their heart, yet so that {{gender:humankind|man}} cannot find out the work that God has done from beginning to end.

R.11: God has made each thing right for its own time. He has also put in people a longing for what lasts forever. But they still cannot understand all that God has done, from the beginning to the end.

decisions.choice: beautiful: fitting, right for its time
decisions.reason: The word (yafeh) usually means beautiful in appearance. Here, with "in its time", it means fitting: each thing has its right time (Proverbs 15:23).

decisions.choice: eternity: a sense of time beyond the present, of the whole that people cannot see
alternatives: ignorance, darkness (from a like-sounding root meaning hidden)
a sense of duration, of the long course of time
decisions.reason: The word ('olam) means a very long time, past or future, and is usually rendered "forever" (1:4; 3:14). Only here does it stand alone, "the 'olam", as something God puts into human hearts, and its sense is debated. Most take it as eternity: God has given people a sense of time beyond the times of verses 1-8, a reach toward the whole, which makes them ask what it all means; yet they cannot grasp it. Others take it in its later Hebrew sense, "the world", or connect it with a root meaning "hidden" ('alam): God has put something hidden in their hearts, so that they cannot find out his work.

decisions.choice: yet so that: people cannot find out God's work
alternatives: without which people could not find out anything
decisions.reason: The words (mibbeli 'asher lo') mean "without that", here "yet in such a way that ... not". The sense of eternity does not let people grasp God's work from beginning to end (8:17).

decisions.choice: a sense of eternity (B); a longing for what lasts forever (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for 'olam here: "eternity" at Literal, "a sense of eternity" at Balanced, "a longing for what lasts forever" at Readable. The reading is uncertain (m2), and each level keeps to the one taken.

decisions.choice: fitting (B); right (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the word here (m1); Literal keeps "beautiful".

decisions.choice: {{gender:humankind|man}}
decisions.reason: The word ('adam) means human beings in general; the gender setting gives the inclusive form by default.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God at the start, where the Hebrew has only the verb.

records.source: יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין ט֖וֹב בָּ֑ם כִּ֣י אִם־לִשְׂמ֔וֹחַ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת ט֖וֹב בְּחַיָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: I know that there is not good in them except to rejoice and to do good in his life.
pieces: I know that there is nothing better for them than to be glad and to do good as long as they live.

L.12: I know that there is nothing good for them except to rejoice and to do good in {{gender:their|his}} life.

R.12: I know that the best thing people can do is to be happy and do good while they are alive.

decisions.choice: nothing good ... except: nothing better than
decisions.reason: The words say there is no good for them but this, which is to say nothing better (2:24).

decisions.choice: to do good: to do what is right, or to enjoy what is good
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "to do good" usually means doing right (7:20). Next to "rejoice", and with verse 13 speaking of seeing good, some take it to mean enjoying oneself. Both readings fit the call to make the most of life as God gives it.

decisions.choice: in his life: the singular after "them"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew moves from "them" to "his life", each person's own life.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The pronoun means each person; the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default.

records.source: וְגַ֤ם כָּל־הָאָדָם֙ שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְרָאָ֥ה ט֖וֹב בְּכָל־עֲמָל֑וֹ מַתַּ֥ת אֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃
records.gloss: And also every man who eats and drinks and sees good in all his toil, a gift of God it [is].
pieces: And also, when anyone eats and drinks and finds enjoyment in all their hard work, it is God's gift.

L.13: And also every {{gender:person|man}} who eats and drinks and sees good in all {{gender:their|his}} toil—it [is] the gift of God.

R.13: When people eat and drink and enjoy their hard work, that is a gift from God.

decisions.choice: the gift of God: enjoyment is given, not earned
decisions.reason: The word (mattat) is a gift. As in 2:24, the good of eating, drinking and working is something God gives (5:18).

decisions.choice: sees good: enjoys
decisions.reason: "To see good" is to enjoy (2:1, 24).

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

records.source: יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּ֠י כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה הָאֱלֹהִים֙ ה֚וּא יִהְיֶ֣ה לְעוֹלָ֔ם עָלָיו֙ אֵ֣ין לְהוֹסִ֔יף וּמִמֶּ֖נּוּ אֵ֣ין לִגְרֹ֑עַ וְהָאֱלֹהִ֣ים עָשָׂ֔ה שֶׁיִּֽרְא֖וּ מִלְּפָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: I know that all which God does, it will be forever; to it not to add and from it not to take away; and God has done [it] that they fear from before him.
pieces: I know that whatever God does lasts forever; nothing can be added to it and nothing taken from it. God has done this so that people will fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.14: I know that all that God does will be forever; to it there is nothing to add, and from it there is nothing to take away; and God has done [this] so that they will fear before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.14: I know that everything God does will last forever. No one can add anything to it or take anything away from it. God does this so that people will honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with awe.

decisions.choice: fear before him: reverent awe of God
decisions.reason: To fear God is to stand in awe of him, taking him seriously as God, as in "the fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge" (Proverbs 1:7). Here it comes from seeing that God's work stands forever while human work passes like a breath. The book returns to it in 5:6, 7:18, 8:12-13 and 12:13.

decisions.choice: nothing to add and nothing to take away
decisions.reason: The same pair of words is used of God's commands in Deuteronomy 4:2 and 13:1: nothing may be added to them or taken from them. God's work is complete as it is.

decisions.choice: forever: it lasts
decisions.reason: The word ('olam) is the one in 3:11. What God does lasts, set against the breath of human toil.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: A pronoun for God takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: honor him with awe
decisions.reason: The settled Readable wording for the fear of God, as in Proverbs 1:7. Literal and Balanced keep "fear".

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who is to fear God, which the Hebrew leaves understood.

records.source: מַה־שֶּֽׁהָיָה֙ כְּבָ֣ר ה֔וּא וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לִהְי֖וֹת כְּבָ֣ר הָיָ֑ה וְהָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת־נִרְדָּֽף׃
records.gloss: What is, already it [was], and what [is] to be, already it has been; and God seeks what is pursued.
pieces: Whatever is has already been, and whatever will be has already been; and God seeks out what has gone by.

L.15: Whatever is has already been, and what is to be has already been; and God seeks what has been driven away.

R.15: Whatever is happening now has happened before, and whatever will happen has happened before. God brings back what has passed.

decisions.choice: God seeks what has been driven away: God calls back what has passed, so that it comes again
alternatives: God seeks out those who are pursued (the persecuted)
God calls the past to account
decisions.reason: The last words are literally "God seeks the pursued". After the first half, which repeats 1:9, most take them to mean that God brings back what time has driven away, so that what was comes round again. Others read "the pursued" as people who are persecuted, whom God takes up, or as past deeds, which God calls to account; that would lead into the judgment of verses 16-17.

decisions.choice: what is has already been: as in 1:9
decisions.reason: The first half echoes 1:9-10: nothing is new.

records.source: וְע֥וֹד רָאִ֖יתִי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ מְק֤וֹם הַמִּשְׁפָּט֙ שָׁ֣מָּה הָרֶ֔שַׁע וּמְק֥וֹם הַצֶּ֖דֶק שָׁ֥מָּה הָרָֽשַׁע׃
records.gloss: And again I saw under the sun: the place of justice, there [was] the wickedness; and the place of righteousness, there [was] the wickedness.
pieces: I saw something else under the sun: in the place of justice there was wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there was wickedness.

L.16: And again I saw under the sun: the place of justice—there [was] wickedness; and the place of righteousness—there [was] wickedness.

R.16: I also saw this here on earth: where there should have been justice, there was evil. Where people should have done what is right, there was evil.

decisions.choice: the place of justice: the courts
decisions.reason: Justice was given at the city gate or before judges (Deuteronomy 17:8; Amos 5:15). The places set apart for justice were where wrong was done.

decisions.choice: wickedness: guilt, injustice
decisions.reason: The word (resha') is the opposite of righteousness; the second time it may also be read "the wicked".

decisions.choice: where there should have been justice ... where people should have done what is right
alternatives: the place of justice ... the place of righteousness
decisions.reason: Readable says what the places were for (m1).

records.source: אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י אֶת־הַצַּדִּיק֙ וְאֶת־הָ֣רָשָׁ֔ע יִשְׁפֹּ֖ט הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים כִּי־עֵ֣ת לְכָל־חֵ֔פֶץ וְעַ֥ל כָּל־הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: I said, I, in my heart: The righteous and the wicked God will judge, for a time [is] for every matter, and on every deed there.
pieces: I said to myself, "God will judge both the righteous and the wicked, since every matter has its time, and every deed its time there."

L.17: I said in my heart, "The righteous and the wicked God will judge, for [there is] a time for every matter, and for every deed, there."

R.17: I said to myself, "God will judge both those who do right and those who do wrong. There is a time for every matter, and for every deed there is a time when God will judge it."

decisions.choice: God will judge the righteous and the wicked
decisions.reason: Against the injustice of verse 16, Qoheleth holds that God will judge. Among the times of verses 1-8 there is a time for judgment, though he does not say when (11:9; 12:14).

decisions.choice: there: with God, at the time of his judgment
alternatives: in the place of justice of verse 16
he has set (a time), reading a word with a different letter
decisions.reason: The last word, "there", is abrupt. It may point to God's judgment, the place and time where every deed is weighed, or back to the courts of verse 16. Some read a different letter and get "he has appointed" a time for every deed.

decisions.choice: I said to myself
decisions.reason: As in 1:16.

decisions.choice: a time when God will judge it
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the reading taken (m2).

records.source: אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י עַל־דִּבְרַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם לְבָרָ֖ם הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְלִרְא֕וֹת שְׁהֶם־בְּהֵמָ֥ה הֵ֖מָּה לָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: I said, I, in my heart concerning the sons of humankind: for God to test them, and to see that they [are] animals, they to themselves.
pieces: I said to myself about human beings, "God is testing them, to show them that they are only animals."

L.18: I said in my heart concerning the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}, "[It is] for God to test them, and to show that they [are] animals, they themselves."

R.18: I also said to myself, "God is testing people to show them that they are only animals."

decisions.choice: test: sift, show what they are
decisions.reason: The verb (barar) means to sift or sort out, to show what is pure (Daniel 11:35). God tests people so that they see what they are.

decisions.choice: to show that they are animals: so that they see that they themselves are like animals
decisions.reason: The verb is "to see". It most likely means that people are to see this for themselves; it could also mean that God sees it. "They themselves" stresses that, left to themselves, people die as animals do (verse 19).

decisions.choice: concerning: on account of
decisions.reason: The word (divrat) means "for the sake of" or "concerning" (7:14; 8:2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}
decisions.reason: The phrase means human beings, men and women; the gender setting gives the inclusive form by default (see 1:13).

decisions.choice: only animals
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "only" for the stress of "they themselves" (m2).

records.source: כִּי֩ מִקְרֶ֨ה בְֽנֵי־הָאָדָ֜ם וּמִקְרֶ֣ה הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה וּמִקְרֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ לָהֶ֔ם כְּמ֥וֹת זֶה֙ כֵּ֣ן מ֣וֹת זֶ֔ה וְר֥וּחַ אֶחָ֖ד לַכֹּ֑ל וּמוֹתַ֨ר הָאָדָ֤ם מִן־הַבְּהֵמָה֙ אָ֔יִן כִּ֥י הַכֹּ֖ל הָֽבֶל׃
records.gloss: For the fate of the sons of humankind and the fate of the animal, and one fate [is] to them; as the death of this, so the death of that, and one spirit [is] to all; and the advantage of the man over the animal [is] nothing, for the all [is] breath.
pieces: For what happens to human beings and what happens to animals is the same: one fate comes to them both. As one dies, so does the other. All of them have the same spirit, and humans have no advantage over animals, for everything is a breath.

L.19: For the fate of the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}} and the fate of the animal—one fate [is] theirs: as this one dies, so that one dies, and one spirit [is] in all; and the advantage of {{gender:humankind|man}} over the animal [is] nothing, for everything [is] breath.

R.19: What happens to people also happens to animals. The same thing happens to both of them: they both die. They all have the same spirit that gives them life. People are not better off than animals. Everything is like a breath that does not last.

decisions.choice: fate: death, which comes to all
decisions.reason: As in 2:14, the word (miqreh) is what befalls a person; the next words say what it is: death.

decisions.choice: spirit: the breath of life that God gives
decisions.reason: The word (ruach) is the life-breath God gives to people and animals alike (Genesis 6:17; 7:22; Psalm 104:29-30); in 12:7 it returns to God who gave it. It is not the word hevel, which this book renders "breath".

decisions.choice: advantage: superiority, what one has over another
decisions.reason: The word (motar) comes from the same root as "gain" (yitron). Proverbs uses it for the profit of hard work (Proverbs 14:23); here, facing death, humans have none over animals.

decisions.choice: breath: brief, soon gone
decisions.reason: Here hevel leans toward the brevity of life (see the note at 1:2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}
decisions.reason: The phrase means human beings, men and women; the gender setting gives the inclusive form by default (see 1:13).

decisions.choice: spirit
decisions.reason: Ruach is rendered "spirit" here so that it is not confused with hevel, which every level renders with "breath".

decisions.choice: like a breath that does not last
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture and gives the sense here (m4).

records.source: הַכֹּ֥ל הוֹלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־מָק֣וֹם אֶחָ֑ד הַכֹּל֙ הָיָ֣ה מִן־הֶֽעָפָ֔ר וְהַכֹּ֖ל שָׁ֥ב אֶל־הֶעָפָֽר׃
records.gloss: The all [is] going to one place; the all was from the dust, and the all [is] returning to the dust.
pieces: Everything goes to the same place: all came from the dust, and all go back to the dust.

L.20: All go to one place; all came from the dust, and all return to the dust.

R.20: People and animals all end up in the same place. They all came from the dust, and they will all go back to the dust.

decisions.choice: from the dust ... to the dust: as in Genesis
decisions.reason: God formed the first human from the dust (Genesis 2:7) and said, "to dust you shall return" (Genesis 3:19). The book returns to it in 12:7.

decisions.choice: one place: the grave, where all the dead go
decisions.reason: The same words come back in 6:6. The place is the grave, the end of every life.

decisions.choice: People and animals
decisions.reason: Readable names who "all" are, from verse 19.

records.source: מִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ ר֚וּחַ בְּנֵ֣י הָאָדָ֔ם הָעֹלָ֥ה הִ֖יא לְמָ֑עְלָה וְר֨וּחַ֙ הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה הַיֹּרֶ֥דֶת הִ֖יא לְמַ֥טָּה לָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Who knows the spirit of the sons of humankind, [whether] it goes up upward, and the spirit of the animal, [whether] it goes down downward to the earth?
pieces: Who knows whether the human spirit rises upward and the spirit of the animal goes down into the earth?

L.21: Who knows [whether] the spirit of the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}} goes up upward, and [whether] the spirit of the animal goes down downward to the earth?

R.21: Who can be sure that a person's spirit goes up, and an animal's spirit goes down into the ground?

decisions.choice: whether it goes up ... whether it goes down: a question
alternatives: the spirit that goes up ... the spirit that goes down (the vowels of the Hebrew text)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew letters can be read "whether it goes up" or "the one that goes up". The vowels of the traditional Hebrew text read the second, so that the verse says the human spirit does go up, though no one knows it. The ancient Greek and other early translations read it as a question, which fits "who knows?" and verse 19. The question is followed here. This description of the ancient translations is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: who knows: no one can see what happens to the spirit at death
decisions.reason: Qoheleth does not deny that the human spirit goes to God; in 12:7 he says that the spirit returns to God who gave it. Here he says that no one can see the difference between the death of a person and the death of an animal.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}
decisions.reason: The phrase means human beings, men and women; the gender setting gives the inclusive form by default (see 1:13).

records.source: וְרָאִ֗יתִי כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין טוֹב֙ מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׂמַ֤ח הָאָדָם֙ בְּֽמַעֲשָׂ֔יו כִּי־ה֖וּא חֶלְק֑וֹ כִּ֣י מִ֤י יְבִיאֶ֨נּוּ֙ לִרְא֔וֹת בְּמֶ֖ה שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And I saw that there is not good more than that the man rejoices in his works, for it [is] his portion; for who will bring him to look on what will be after him?
pieces: So I saw that there is nothing better for people than to rejoice in their work, for that is their share. For who can bring them to see what will happen after them?

L.22: So I saw that there is nothing better than that {{gender:a person|a man}} should rejoice in {{gender:their|his}} works, for that [is] {{gender:their|his}} portion; for who will bring {{gender:them|him}} to see what will be after {{gender:them|him}}?

R.22: So I saw that the best thing people can do is to enjoy their work. That is what life gives them. After all, who can show them what will happen after they are gone?

decisions.choice: portion: the share given to enjoy now (see 2:10)
decisions.reason: The word (cheleq) is the share of life a person has now.

decisions.choice: what will be after him: what will happen on earth after he is gone
decisions.reason: The same words in 6:12 and 7:14 mean what will happen under the sun after a person dies. No one can see it, so the present share is what a person has.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: share (B); what life gives them (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for cheleq (see 2:10).
